16.t: Working with data: air pressure and height
q: Read the air pressure at 4 km.
Calculate the drop in pressure from 0 to 2 km and from 10 to 12 km.
Explain why air pressure falls with height.
Higher up there is less air above pushing down, and the air is less dense.
Planes cruise at about 11 km. Explain why their cabins are pressurised.
At 11 km the pressure is only about 22 kPa (a fifth of sea level): too little oxygen enters the blood each breath, so people would pass out. The cabin is pumped to about 75 kPa.
